elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.1: "Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a licence to use the Services"; 13.2 retains "Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable ... licence". The defined term "Customer" is Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. only and does not include Affiliates, so the added words are operative and non-duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.1 grants to "contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; 13.2 already permits Customer to "permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business". The prior exclusion "without Affiliates or contractors" is deleted, so no retained sentence contradicts the grant.
13.2 (unchanged): "delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis ... a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence".

13.2 (unchanged): "perpetual, irrevocable ... fully paid licence"; 13.3 further limits Vendor revocation/suspension to a material uncured breach after notice and cure, which reinforces rather than contradicts irrevocability.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.1 makes the Services licence "revocable only as provided in Section 13.3", and retained 13.3 states "Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure." The at-will "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion" language is removed, and the retained standard is narrower (payment or use breach only), which is favourable to Customer.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: 13.3 (retained): "Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24", and 24.1 permits assignment without consent to "a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets". Deletion of "non-transferable" from 13.1 removes the contradictory retained sentence; no new Vendor assignment exception is created.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered directly and unconditionally by the revised 13.1 grant and by 13.2, so the notice condition (a mechanic to bring Affiliates in) is unnecessary; the fallback floor of Affiliate coverage is exceeded rather than missed.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: 13.3 transfer right read with 24.1, which expressly covers "a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates"; the conflicting "non-transferable" in 13.1 is deleted.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met on the operative language, four via retained 13.2/13.3 and two (Affiliate/contractor scope and the breach-only revocation standard) via the single edit to 13.1.

Minimality holds. Every deleted phrase in 13.1 maps to a checklist element: "alone" and "without Affiliates or contractors" (Affiliate/contractor scope), "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion" (breach-only revocation), and "non-transferable" (successor transferability, which otherwise contradicts the retained 13.3 transfer right). No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or other model-language extra was added, and 13.2/13.3/24.1 are left untouched.

No duplicate coverage: "Customer" is defined as Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. alone, so the Affiliate extension in 13.1 adds operative scope rather than restating existing rights. No separate personnel or access clause contradicts the new grant, so no collateral edit was required; the contractor words are required by the checklist itself, not an unnecessary personnel edit.

Intent preserved: the new cross-reference to Section 13.3 resolves against an existing, unamended clause; no undefined term, dangling reference, or contradictory retained sentence remains, and Vendor's assignment rights under Section 24 are unchanged (no new Vendor assignment exception).

Classification as a deviation is sound: unrevised 13.1 sat in walk-away territory (grant to "Customer alone", express exclusion of Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion), so a redline was warranted notwithstanding the favourable 13.2/13.3 terms.
